Tara S.: Heads up — after the kernel+driver roll on GCP us-west we're seeing weird tail latency on the same A100v4 SKU compared to AWS eu-west. Filing here so eng-ml can triage.
Oya K.: Can you paste the minimal repro and the exact driver/kernel/CUDA versions?
Tara S.: Repro command: `./bench.sh --model=redwood-13b --batch=1 --seq=1024 --iters=200`
Stack GCP node: driver=535.104, CUDA=12.1, kernel=6.1. AWS node: driver=555.23, CUDA=12.2, kernel=6.6
Tara S.: Quick logs snapshot:
```
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version,gpu_name,clocks.gr --format=csv
"A100-SXM4-80GB", 535.104, 1410
```
Oya K.: Huh. AWS has newer driver but lower tail latency? what are the numbers?
Tara S.: GCP us-west: p50=18ms p95=78ms p99=230ms. AWS eu-west: p50=16ms p95=24ms p99=60ms. (same binary + q4_0 quant)
Mike L.: Saw similar on Azure last month — clock governor differences caused turbo not to engage consistently. Did you check cpufreq / governor and power capping?
Tara S.: Good call. On GCP `scaling_governor` was `powersave`. On AWS it's `performance`. Also found dmesg entry: `nvidia: GPU clock throttled due to thermal limit` even though GPU temp ~68C.
Samir P.: Thermal messages at 68C are weird — could be driver/firmware discrepancy in sensor mapping. Also check MIG slices and NVLINK peer settings; different clouds sometimes ship different firmware.
ci-bot: deploy: kernel=6.6.0-rc rolled to gcp-us-west-2a (hosts: infra-ml-*)
Oya K.: Can you run these on one of the problematic GCP machines? `sudo cat /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpufreq/policy*/scaling_governor` and `dmesg | grep -i nvidia` Also `nvidia-smi --query-supported-clocks`
Tara S.: Ran them and pasted output to the infra gist (link): https://redwood/gists/clk-gcp-output (short: governor=powersave, supported clocks list shorter than AWS)
Mike L.: If supported clocks differ it could be a vendor firmware/profile causing reduced boost bins. Also driver version mismatches can flip thermal/clock policies.
Oya K.: Plan: 1) spin canary images with identical driver 555 + CUDA 12.2 on GCP and AWS 2) run microbench with NVTX and perf counters 3) test toggling governor + explicit clock override and power capping 4) evaluate with q8 quant as well to see mem access pattern impact
Tara S.: I'll run step 1 tomorrow. Quick note — p95 regression only shows up for batch=1 and seq>=512, batch=4 is fine (so might be scheduler/clock ramp latency).
Samir P.: Also check kernel release config: CONFIG_THERMAL, cpufreq governors, and cgroup.latency sensitivity on the images. Different cloud images patch kernels differently.
Mike L.: I'll own perf counters and telemetry traces. Adding a small script to sweep clocks and log p50/p95: `bench_clock_sweep.py` (will post soon).
Tara S.: Filed incident INC-2026-234 and linked canary run. Assigning to @Oya K. and @Mike L. :eyes:
Oya K.: Taking it. Will report back with canary numbers and NV counters.
Mike L.: ETA EOD PST for perf traces.
Tara S.: Thanks — ping me if you need a repro image. :thumbsup:
